newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks mixed, market stability to last.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks mixed, market stability to last.

text.p: Croatian stocks were mixed in meagre trading on Friday, with some leading issues untraded, but traders predicted further steady gains for most shares.
"The growth will continue. I can not see the upward trend end yet," said Velimir Zelimorski from the Fima brokerage.
He said a growing number of foreign investors as well as Croatian citizens investing their savings could also propel the market.
"Spectacular gains in the past few months and the media attention that followed will keep the interest high," Zelimorski said.
He predicted fully listed Zagrebacka banka and pharmaceutical company Pliva would fluctuate around the present value.
* Of eight active issues, five were up, one down, one flat and one was traded for the first time this year.
* Most actively traded was fully listed Zagrebacka banka, losing 40 kuna to 970 with 1,543 shares traded.
* Biggest gainer confectioner Kras closed at 660 kuna, gaining 40, on volume of 657 units.
* The Istrian hoteliers kept up their upward trend.
- Jadranturist went up 40 kuna to close at 415, on a volume of 238 shares.
- Arenaturist edged up 15 kuna to reach 210, with 332 shares traded.
- Laguna remained flat at 1,000 kuna, with 170 shares sold.
* Another hotelier Suncani Hvar went up five kuna to close at 50 with 836 shares changing hands.
* Food processor Podravka up 3.5 kuna to 278, selling 528.
* Liquor producer Badel was traded for the first time this year, selling 300 shares at 88,75 kuna.
* Daily share volume down to 4,604, total turnover higher at 2.5 million kuna.
